items.text: Another day in the snow. The colony holds, for now.
A new round begins. The cold has not moved on.
The last round. Whatever happens now, happens now.
The colony meets a crisis. Hand in what you can spare.
Something has gone wrong again. Cards go in, face down.
The colony weathers it. Barely.
It was not enough. The colony pays for it.
The dead have reached the gate.
The stores run dry, and the colony goes hungry.
Morale is almost gone. People are watching each other.
A vote has been called. Someone here is not trusted.
Three. Two. One.
Exiled. The door closes behind them, and the cold takes the rest.
Not enough votes. They stay, and they will remember.
The colony's goal is met. Hold on to it.
The colony falls. The winter takes everyone who stayed.
You made it through the winter, and you were not alone.
Some people left the colony alive. You were not among them.
Eight weeks of darkness. Outlast the winter, and be still standing when the last day ends.
Kill them. Thin out the dead until only a handful are left walking.
Find a cure. Gather medicine, enough for everyone who set out, and bring it home.
Home sweet home. Board up the colony, and every other place, until nothing gets through.
Raiding party. Strip two other places bare before the cold takes them.
Leave it all behind. Arm everyone, stock the food, and be ready to run.
Stockpile. Fill the supply, bar the doors, and hoard enough to last.
Winter has come. Keep feeding the fire, or the cold will finish this.
Too many mouths. Five rounds. Hold out for five rounds.
We need more samples. Every dead one may carry something worth taking.
Another night. The fire is low, the gate is thin, and someone in this room is lying.
Another night. The fire is low, the gate is thin, and someone in this room is lying.
Another night. The fire is low, the gate is thin, and someone in this room is lying.

Annaleigh is in the old holding block with the cell keys in her hand and one name she cannot stop repeating. What she does with the next few minutes will tell the colony what kind of person she turned out to be.
The feral kids have trailed Arthur for blocks, a ragged line of faces with nothing behind the eyes. They close in around the cart he is guarding, and he knows how this ends whichever way he leans.

Bev stops at the school gate without meaning to, and the playground swing is still moving. Someone small is waiting in the shadow of the stairwell, and she has to decide what she can live with before she takes another step.

Ice has sealed the seams of the doorframe and the wind keeps trying every gap. Behind the door a small group has a stove barely warm enough to matter, and outside a half-frozen traveller is scratching at the wood.

Inside a locked case at the back of the library sits a huge hand-lettered volume with a cracked spine. It is heavy enough to be a weapon and odd enough to be a treasure, and you only have room in your pack for one idea of what it is for.
Brian pins a sketched floor plan to the wall and calls the whole colony to look. He says the colony has been scraping by on bad luck, and that tonight it can start taking what it needs.
The house Carla is combing is not as empty as it looked from the road. Something in a stained coat paces the upper landing, one hand resting on a holster, and its head turns slowly toward the stairs.
Someone has tied scraps of foil to a coat rack and called it a tree. When an old cook asks if the stores can spare a real meal for one evening, the whole hall holds its breath.
A collapsed lean-to rattles and a gaunt woman bursts from it with a length of rebar and nothing in her eyes that you can reason with. She is guarding a stash under the planks.

David has audited the stores three nights running, and the numbers refuse to close. Either someone is quietly pocketing rations, or he has made a mistake in front of everyone, and he has to commit to one of those stories now.
The evidence room has two containers still sealed: a battered cooler and a steel drum. Whichever one you pry open, something inside is going to scream back at you.

The wound is too clean to be a bite. It is a burn across the ribs where a bullet skimmed past, and the tracks in the snow beyond the hedge belong to boots, not shuffling feet. Somebody is out there, patient and warm, and they have chosen the colony as their quarry.
On the long road a lone shape is limping forward with a loose crowd of the dead behind her. The lookout knows the walk before the face, and the rifle is already up.

Tiny boot prints cross the stairwell dust and end at a boiler room door. When the survivor calls out, a handful of faces appear behind a stack of crates, quiet and watchful, as if they have practised hiding for a long time.

Two people who shared a tent for weeks start trading the kind of accusations that cannot be unsaid, in the open, with the whole block listening. One of them will have to give ground before the dead decide for them.

The freezer aisle still hums with cold, and one stocked shelf looks untouched since the last delivery. A faded hand-painted sign above it says take only what you need, and for some reason it makes the survivor think of Maude.

Two shifts collide in the supply corridor and a shoving match turns ugly when one of them starts listing who does not belong here. Voices rally behind him from the back, and for a moment the colony looks ready to split along lines the world already erased. It falls to the table to say what kind of place this will be.

Marlow stopped eating on Tuesday, and by Friday there is a blistered rash climbing his arms and a smell in the dormitory that people are trying not to name. Two cots away, a child has started to cough. The table must say what happens to the ones who cannot defend themselves.
A rusted truck idles at the gate with its lights off, its bed crowded with silent faces under blankets. The driver steps down slowly, hands open, and asks whether there is room for a winter.

In a corner of the hospital activity room waits a karaoke machine, a crate of board games and three working car batteries. It is enough to put on a real party for the colony, if you do not mind the noise.
